claude_only.name: Which authoritative registry entry establishes this scheme, and under what key?
What class of referents may be named under this scheme, and what is explicitly excluded?
What namespace expression must accompany a value of this scheme when it is carried inside another model?
Is the scheme versioned, and does a version change alter the meaning of identifiers already assigned?
What is the scheme's registration status and when did that status last change?
Which characters and encodings are permitted, and how is case treated?
Which substrings of an identifier are structurally significant, and what do they delimit?
What minimum and maximum lengths apply, and are they enforced at assignment or only at validation?
How are historical values that fail the current grammar handled?
What check character algorithm applies, and over which part of the string is it computed?
What does a passing check prove, and what does it not prove?
Which authority must be consulted to confirm that a well-formed identifier has actually been assigned?
If the scheme has no check element, what compensating control detects transcription error?
What is the canonical form of an identifier of this scheme, and how is it derived?
Which transformations preserve identity for this scheme and which must never be applied?
Which comparison level is a consumer entitled to rely on without contacting the authority?
Which form is stored and indexed, and is the form as received also retained?
Does the scheme permit more than one identifier for the same referent, and how are aliases declared?
What may an agent legitimately infer from the structure of an identifier of this scheme?
What must an agent never infer from an identifier value, even when the pattern appears to support it?
What does the identifier disclose to an observer who holds only the string?
If an embedded attribute of the referent changes, does the identifier change?
Who holds the mandate for this scheme, and under what instrument was it granted?
Which body oversees the mandate holder, and what powers does it hold?
How are issuing bodies accredited, and how is accreditation withdrawn?
What evidence supports the mandate holder's ability to sustain the scheme over its intended horizon?
What happens to assignments and resolution if the mandate holder ceases to operate?
How is allocation authority subdivided, and what is the shape of the delegation tree?
Is a delegated namespace portion exclusive, and does it foreclose overlapping allocations?
Who is the change controller for a given registry entry or delegated namespace?
On what grounds can a delegation be revoked, and what becomes of identifiers already issued under it?
May a delegate sub-delegate further, and is the parent bound by the delegate's policy?
Which allocation policy governs new registrations under this scheme?
If review is required, who performs it and against what published criteria?
Which value ranges are reserved, private-use, experimental or otherwise withheld from allocation?
Can the allocation policy itself be changed, and by what procedure?
How does the scheme record values known to be in use without a registration?
Which registration template fields were filed, and which mandatory fields are missing or empty?
Where is the permanent and readily available public specification for this scheme?
What security and privacy analysis was filed with the registration?
How is a registry entry deprecated or obsoleted, and what annotation survives?
Which referent is bound by this assignment, and how is that referent itself identified?
Who performed the assignment, under which delegated authority?
When did the assignment take effect, and when was it recorded?
What evidence supports that the referent is what the registrant claims it to be?
What metadata or conduct obligations does the registrant accept as a condition of assignment?
What is the intended use of this identifier relative to any others held by the same referent?
What is the complete state vocabulary for an identifier under this scheme?
Which state transitions are permitted, and who may trigger each one?
What must a consumer do when an identifier it holds becomes deprecated or retired?
Does the scheme impose a renewal or revalidation duty, and what happens if it lapses?
How does a consumer determine the current state of an identifier, and how fresh is that answer?
Does this scheme permit a retired identifier to be bound to a different referent?
If reuse is permitted, what quarantine period and preconditions apply?
When custody of the referent transfers, does the identifier travel with it?
How are splits and merges of the referent expressed in identifier terms?
How can a consumer detect that an identifier it holds now denotes a different referent?
What is the theoretical capacity of this namespace under its current grammar?
What is the observed allocation rate, and what is the projected exhaustion date?
How can capacity be extended without invalidating existing identifiers?
For probabilistically generated identifiers, what collision probability is accepted and on what basis?
Is resolution intended for this scheme at all, and what did the registration state?
Which services resolve identifiers of this scheme, over which protocols?
What portion of the namespace does each resolver actually cover?
Are resolution parameters or service requests supported, and with what standardised semantics?
What service level, caching guidance and rate limits govern resolution at volume?
Does holding a well-formed identifier of this scheme guarantee any access to the referent?
What may a consumer conclude when resolution fails?
Is the scheme's own namespace expression intended to be dereferenceable?
Does successful resolution establish that the returned resource is the intended referent?
Who makes the persistence commitment for a given identifier, and are they the current provider?
Which of identifier validity, object availability, content invariance and change history are actually promised?
Over what horizon does the commitment run, and what backs it?
What is returned once the referent is withdrawn, and is its metadata retained?
How is the commitment transferred if custody of the referent or the resolver changes?
What does a successful resolution return, and is it a single value or a typed set?
How does a client request descriptive metadata or a policy statement rather than the referent?
What outcome classes must a client distinguish, and how are they signalled?
What must be recorded about a resolution so that the result can be reproduced or disputed later?
What relation type does this mapping assert, and is it symmetric or transitive?
What is the quality of this mapping and how was it measured?
May this mapping be chained with others to infer a further correspondence?
How is a mapping withdrawn when one side is deprecated or reassigned?
What cardinality does the mapping have, and how are one-to-many correspondences represented?
What must accompany an identifier value for a consumer to interpret it without external context?
Are abbreviations or prefixes permitted in carriage, and is their scope local only?
When a referent holds several identifiers, how is the preferred one designated?
How is the period during which an identifier was valid for the referent recorded?
How is the assigning body recorded alongside the value?
What counts as a collision under this scheme, and how is one detected?
When two identifiers are found to denote the same referent, which survives and how is the other marked?
How is use of unregistered or squatted values discovered and handled?
When an upstream source standard changes a code, how does the scheme absorb the change?
What signal lets a consumer detect that stored values no longer match the scheme in force?
Which standard, edition and clause does this scheme claim conformance to, and what evidence supports the claim?
What defect rate is observed in the assignment register, and how is it measured?
Who audits the scheme's operation, how often, and what are the published findings?
What is the remediation path when a defect or non-conformance is found?
Which external standards are aligned with but not conformed to, and where do they diverge?
Are values of this scheme personal data, directly or through re-identification?
What does a value disclose about its referent or its creation to a party holding only the string?
Can the namespace be enumerated or harvested, and what controls limit that?
Is the value ever accepted as evidence of authorisation or identity, and how is that prevented?
How is an erasure or restriction request reconciled with a persistence commitment?
Does any national or sectoral restriction limit processing of this identifier?
Under what legal instrument does the scheme operate, and in which jurisdictions is it effective?
On what terms may the registry, assignment register and crosswalk data be used and redistributed?
What ongoing obligations bind a registrant, and what are the fees?
Who inherits the scheme, its register and its resolution duty if the operator winds down?
Who holds change control over the scheme record and over individual entries?

grok_only.name: What is the authoritative master-system identifier of this scheme in IANA, ISO, W3C, GS1 or another registration authority, and which registry record is canonical?
What governed global IRI or URN identifies the scheme definition itself when the master registry uses a local token?
If no master-system identifier exists, what UUID or ULID did the adopting Dimension assign, and when was that assignment observed?
What official names, abbreviations and alternate labels must be preserved without treating them as identifiers?
Is this scheme a URI scheme, URN namespace, DID method, ISO/IEC 6523 organisation-identification scheme, UUID generator, GS1 key, PID framework, or another classified naming system?
What stated purpose and long-lived utility does the scheme registration claim, and which resource class may receive identifiers?
Does the scheme function as a persistent name, a locator, both, or neither, and is default dereference required to be safe?
In which protocols, industries or communities is the scheme intended to be used, and is use outside that context invalid or merely unsupported?
Which check-digit or check-character algorithm applies, is the check symbol part of the identifier value, and which keys are exempt?
Which reserved characters act as delimiters inside the scheme-specific part, and when must they be percent-encoded rather than used as data?
Are identifiers required to be opaque, may they be semantic, and is a transcription-safe alphabet recommended?
What normalisation steps are mandatory before declaring two values URN-equivalent, URI-equivalent or scheme-equivalent, and which components are ignored?
What is the single canonical serialisation producers MUST emit, including lowercase scheme names and uppercase percent-hex?
Which compact, fully qualified, hyphenated, rendered-value or human-display forms are allowed, and which form is used for computational matching?
How does the scheme treat homoglyphs, mixed-script lookalikes and visually identical Unicode that are not octet-equal after normalisation?
Which organisation is the registration authority or designated expert body, and what is its master-system identifier in the party register?
What instrument, standard clause or IANA policy mandates this authority, and from when does the mandate run?
Which evaluation criteria, uniqueness guarantees and publication duties does the authority actually perform?
What happens to the scheme and its assignments if the registration authority is reassigned, loses a domain name used in private schemes, or is dissolved?
What is the current registration status and which procedure (expert review, first-come first-served, IESG approval or fast-track for SDOs) admitted it?
Where is the required security and privacy analysis, including whether the scheme-specific part is privacy-sensitive or correlating?
Which template fields are complete, which are missing, and is a citable specification required for this status?
What prefix, NAAN, ICD, Handle naming authority or OID arc was delegated, to whom, and under which parent namespace?
Is the Name Assigning Authority distinct from the Name Mapping Authority or resolver operator, and what URL is the official resolver for this delegation?
Under what conditions can a prefix be reassigned or revoked, and how are already-minted identifiers protected?
What evidence shows that assignments under this delegation cannot collide with siblings?
Who may update the scheme definition, syntax or resolution behaviour, and which updates require IESG, ISO or RA approval?
Does a successor scheme replace, encapsulate or sit alongside this one, and how are old identifiers rewritten or aliased?
Which previously valid identifiers remain valid after a syntax modernisation, as RFC 8141 promises for RFC 2141 URNs?
Is assignment performed by a registrar, by a local minter under a delegated prefix, by a public algorithm, or by a DID method on a verifiable data registry?
Who assigned the identifier, at what event time, and when was that fact ingested, with evidence?
Under what contract, fee, eligibility or persistence commitment did the registrant obtain the assignment?
If the identifier is derived from a name in another namespace, what canonical octets, hash and Namespace ID were used?
Is uniqueness global, scoped to a namespace, scoped to an assigner, or only statistically probable as with UUIDs?
May one referent hold multiple identifiers in this scheme, and may one identifier ever denote a set or time-varying mapping?
Are identifiers unique only within a local system URI, as in FHIR Identifier.system, or globally unique as assigned-names?
What catalogue identifier of the referent is bound, and in which sibling model does that referent live?
If this is a DID or similar, is the controller distinct from the subject, and who may update the binding?
What evidence quality and provenance attach to the claim that this identifier denotes that referent?
At what granularity is the identifier defined, and may finer parts be addressed by qualifiers or fragments rather than new assignments?
If a notation or code is used, is it unique only within a concept scheme, and what URI or URN is the preferred computational identifier?
Do content-negotiated, language, format or version variants share the assigned name or require distinct identifiers?
What is the current status or use of this identifier, and is that status a modifier that changes matching behaviour?
If the identifier is temporary, what replacement is expected, and may systems persist it beyond the stated period?
Who is authorised to change status, and what evidence is required for retirement or deactivation?
During which inclusive start and end instants is or was this identifier valid for use, and is a missing end interpreted as ongoing?
Which versionId or versionTime selects the representation that was current at a past instant?
What is the event time of the lifecycle change versus the observation or ingestion time of this record?
Does retirement mean the name remains reserved forever, becomes a tombstone that resolves only to metadata, is deactivated, or may be recycled after a cooling-off period?
If reassignment is permitted, what event bound the retired identifier to a new referent, and what collision checks were performed?
Is physical deletion of the assignment record allowed, or must a deactivated or old identifier remain queryable for matching and audit?
If two identifiers were merged, which value survives, which are aliases, and is the merge reversible?
If one identifier was split, which new identifiers were minted for which new referents, and what is the parent identifier?
Are multiple identifiers for one referent true aliases, purpose-specific identifiers, or embeddings of another scheme?
What is the resolver endpoint URI, protocol and operator, and is it the official resolver registered for this prefix or NAAN?
Which scheme partitions, prefixes or identifier classes does this resolver cover, and what happens for identifiers outside coverage?
Which operations besides default dereference are defined, including retrieval, metadata, inflections and Handle admin, and which is the default safe operation?
What service level, availability and update-freshness commitments apply to DOI records or equivalent mappings?
Does this scheme define r-component or equivalent resolver parameters, or are they still undefined and therefore not to be used?
Which DID URL parameters are supported to select service, relative resource, version or hash integrity?
Which inputs must be part of the identifier URL and which must be resolver options that are not part of identity?
To which locators, services or metadata records does this identifier currently resolve, and in what type slots?
If multiple targets exist, how is selection performed by content negotiation, country or service parameter, and is order significant?
What integrity and security controls prevent malicious or accidental modification of PID-to-URI mappings?
Who may obtain a representation versus metadata versus a mere existence check, and under which exception process?
If the scheme is not intended as a locator, what does software that obtains the identifier do instead of retrieval?
How are not-found, gone, unauthorised and resolver-unavailable distinguished in logs without treating them as identifier invalidity?
Which from-scheme identifier is mapped to which to-scheme identifier, in which direction, and with what match quality?
Does this mapping conflict with another mapping, with SKOS integrity conditions, or with a merge record in either scheme?
Does this identifier embed another scheme native string, and what canonicalisation is applied before embedding?
Can the native identifier be recovered losslessly from the encapsulating form, and which form is canonical for matching?
Does the encapsulating scheme claim to replace the native scheme, contrary to ISO 26324 non-replacement rule?
Is an IRI form defined, which Unicode characters are allowed before percent-encoding, and is UTF-8 mandatory on the wire?
What compact or prefix expansion is recognised, and who governs the prefix registry?
Which alternate serialisations (URN, OID, braces, integer, binary) are accepted as the same UUID or identifier?
What absolute namespace URI is the system, and what value is unique within it?
Is a coded identifier type recorded for when the system is unknown, without treating type as a substitute for system?
What normalisation is allowed before matching, and is case-insensitive comparison actually safe for this system?

requirements: Resolve every provider-only bundle, layer and finding against primary evidence.
Resolve the model boundary and entry kind before accepting structure.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Record every rejected and deferred node with a reason.
Do not publish while any critical conflict remains unresolved.
